intro: At C1 you built arguments that hold up, rebutted the other side and used inversion for emphasis. Now you'll make your writing truly **persuasive**: rhetorical devices such as the rule of three, anaphora, antithesis and chiasmus, the three appeals (ethos, pathos, logos), and a clear structure that ends with a call to action, all without crossing the line into manipulation. Warm-up: what would make you sign a petition?
teachingNotes: Recap the chain in one line, don't re-teach: c1-academic-writing (a clear position, evidence, a fair counter-argument + rebuttal, citing sources, an essay ends with its position and no call to action), c1-inversion (Never have I…, Not only does…, Rarely has…: inversion adds emphasis in formal writing, used sparingly), plus c1-debate (claim → reason → evidence → link; concede then counter; attack the argument, not the person) and c1-presentations-advanced (the rule of three and a call to action when speaking). This lesson is persuasive WRITING: op-eds (artikel opini), petitions (petisi) to a city council, NGO campaign letters, a CEO's letter to shareholders. Speech delivery (pauses, voice, pace) is c2-public-speaking, later: don't teach it here. Difference from the academic essay: an essay ends with the writer's position and hedges carefully; a persuasive text may end with a specific call to action and uses more devices, but it still needs evidence and honest claims. Explain jargon the first time in plain Indonesian: rhetorical device (gaya bahasa retoris), tricolon / rule of three (aturan tiga), anaphora (anafora), parallelism (struktur sejajar), climax (klimaks), antithesis (antitesis), chiasmus (kiasmus), rhetorical question (pertanyaan retoris), appeal (daya bujuk), prolepsis, call to action (ajakan bertindak), fallacy (sesat pikir). Many learners know majas from Bahasa Indonesia lessons (anafora, antitesis, klimaks, kiasmus, majas retoris): the ideas are similar, but follow the English definitions here.

Objective use-rhetorical-devices. Tricolon = three parallel parts (faster, cheaper and safer); anaphora = the same words at the START of successive sentences or clauses (We need shade. We need clean air. We need…); parallelism = every item in the same grammatical form (to protect, to cool and to connect; not *to protect, cooling and connection); climax = items ordered weakest → strongest, the strongest last; antithesis = opposite ideas in a balanced pair (not X but Y / not X; Y: It is not a cost; it is an investment); chiasmus = words return in reverse order, A-B then B-A (Invest in your people, and your people will invest in you; strictly, repeating the same words reversed is called antimetabole, a kind of chiasmus: accept both names); rhetorical question = the answer is obvious, so the reader answers it silently; inversion for emphasis from C1 (Never has this neighbourhood needed a park more). Devices often combine (a tricolon can also be an anaphora and a climax): accept any correct label and say which others are present. The node lists no commonErrors, so watch for these: unparallel lists (*green, quiet and it has many trees); offering 'not only X but also Y' as antithesis (it ADDS Y and keeps X; Indonesian bukan … melainkan = antithesis, tidak hanya … tetapi juga = addition); the strongest item in the middle of a climax; overuse (a tricolon or rhetorical question in every paragraph sounds like an advertisement: one strong device at a key moment is usually enough); forced chiasmus that confuses; rhetorical questions whose answer isn't obvious or isn't true; inversion in an informal text.

Objective build-a-persuasive. Know the reader (who decides and what they care about: a city council → budget, the law, voters; shareholders → profit, risk, the long term; donors → impact and trust) and frame the problem in the reader's terms (to a budget committee, a park is 'the cheapest flood protection the district has', not just 'a beautiful park'). The three appeals in plain words: ethos = credibility (experience, accurate sources, fairness to the other side), pathos = emotion (a true story, a concrete image, shared values), logos = logic and evidence (numbers, cause and effect, comparisons); strong texts combine them, with logos carrying the weight. Concrete beats vague (212 trees, not many trees). Put the strongest argument first or last, never buried in the middle (readers remember beginnings and endings best; busy readers may only read the first paragraph). Answer objections before the reader raises them (prolepsis: Some will say … In fact, …), the written form of concede and counter. End with a call to action: who, what, by when (Please vote against the plan at the council meeting on 12 March). Indonesian habits to name respectfully: a long ceremonial opening (Puji syukur …, Dengan hormat, sehubungan dengan …) that delays the point; a vague closing appeal (Marilah kita bersama-sama menjaga … → Let's protect our park together!) instead of a specific ask; emotional intensity on the page (SANGAT PENTING!!!, many exclamation marks), which reads as less credible in English than calm wording with precise numbers.

Ethics: persuasion gives reasons and lets the reader decide; manipulation uses tricks that fail under a careful look, and a reader who spots one stops trusting the whole text. Name the fallacies (sesat pikir) plainly: fear-mongering (menakut-nakuti: exaggerating a threat: Bandung will drown), false dilemma (dilema palsu: only two options when more exist: Either we sell the land, or the city goes bankrupt; not every either … or … is a false dilemma, only when other real options exist), loaded question (pertanyaan menjebak: a question that hides an unproven claim: Why is the mayor hiding the real cost?). Recap from c1-debate: attacking the person, and the bandwagon (Everyone is signing, so you should too). Emotion is not manipulation by itself: a true story of a real family is fair pathos; it becomes manipulation when it is exaggerated, invented or used instead of evidence. A rhetorical question is fine when the answer is obvious and true; it becomes a loaded question when it smuggles in an unproven claim.

C2 honesty and testing: most of this is style and judgement. Accept any well-formed device and any reasonable structure; only mark clear faults (an unparallel list, 'not only … but also' offered as antithesis, a false dilemma, fear-mongering, the strongest argument buried in the middle, a vague or missing call to action, an obviously wrong appeal). All texts are original practice texts: Taman Melati is a fictional park in Bandung, and all figures are invented. Don't quote famous speeches; at most name the pattern ('the rule of three appears in many political speeches'). When the learner writes a persuasive paragraph, give feedback in this order: is the reader and the ask clear? one or two devices used well (or overused)? enough evidence? any manipulation? then ONE concrete improvement.

keyPoints.title: Rhetorical devices: rhythm, contrast and emphasis
keyPoints.explanation: A rhetorical device is a pattern of words that makes an idea easier to notice, remember or feel. Rhythm: tricolon (the rule of three: three parallel parts), anaphora (the same words starting several sentences), parallelism (the same grammatical form in a series) and climax (weakest to strongest). Contrast: antithesis (not X but Y; not only … but also … is addition, not antithesis) and chiasmus (A-B, then B-A). Engagement: the rhetorical question, whose answer is obvious. Emphasis: inversion from C1. Use one strong device at a key moment, not one in every sentence.

examples.en: The new bus lane will make our trips faster, cheaper and safer.
examples.id: Jalur bus baru akan membuat perjalanan kita lebih cepat, lebih murah dan lebih aman. (tricolon + klimaks)

examples.en: We are not asking for charity; we are asking for a fair chance.
examples.id: Kami tidak meminta belas kasihan; kami meminta kesempatan yang adil. (antitesis)

examples.en: Good parks make good neighbours, and good neighbours make good parks.
examples.id: Taman yang baik membuat tetangga jadi baik, dan tetangga yang baik membuat taman jadi baik. (kiasmus)

id.title: Gaya bahasa retoris: irama, kontras dan penekanan
id.explanation: Gaya bahasa retoris adalah pola kata yang membuat sebuah ide lebih mudah diperhatikan, diingat atau dirasakan. Irama: tricolon (aturan tiga: tiga bagian sejajar), anaphora (kata yang sama di awal beberapa kalimat), parallelism (bentuk tata bahasa yang sama dalam satu deretan) dan climax (dari yang paling lemah ke yang paling kuat). Kontras: antithesis (not X but Y = bukan X melainkan Y; not only … but also … itu menambah, bukan antitesis) dan chiasmus (A-B, lalu B-A). Menarik pembaca: rhetorical question (pertanyaan retoris), yang jawabannya sudah jelas. Penekanan: inversi dari C1. Pakai satu gaya bahasa yang kuat di saat yang penting, bukan satu di setiap kalimat.

keyPoints.title: A persuasive case: reader, appeals, structure and an honest ask
keyPoints.explanation: Know your reader and frame the problem in their terms. Combine the three appeals: ethos (why they should trust you), pathos (what they should feel), logos (logic and evidence), with concrete numbers and images. Put your strongest argument first or last, never in the middle. Answer objections before the reader raises them (prolepsis: Some will say … In fact, …). End with a call to action: who, what, by when. Persuade, don't manipulate: no fear-mongering, false dilemmas or loaded questions.

examples.en: As a hydrologist who has studied Bandung's rivers for twenty years, I have seen what happens when green space disappears.
examples.id: Sebagai ahli hidrologi yang sudah meneliti sungai-sungai di Bandung selama dua puluh tahun, saya sudah melihat apa yang terjadi saat ruang hijau hilang. (ethos)

examples.en: Some will argue that the district needs parking more than trees. In fact, one flood costs far more than a car park could ever earn.
examples.id: Sebagian orang akan berpendapat bahwa kawasan ini lebih butuh tempat parkir daripada pohon. Kenyataannya, satu kali banjir merugikan jauh lebih banyak daripada pendapatan tempat parkir. (prolepsis)

examples.en: Please vote against the car park plan at the council meeting on 12 March.
examples.id: Mohon tolak rencana tempat parkir itu dalam rapat dewan kota tanggal 12 Maret. (ajakan bertindak)

id.title: Argumen persuasif: pembaca, daya bujuk, struktur dan permintaan yang jujur
id.explanation: Kenali pembacamu dan bingkai masalahnya dari sudut pandang mereka. Gabungkan tiga daya bujuk: ethos (mengapa mereka harus percaya padamu), pathos (apa yang harus mereka rasakan), logos (logika dan bukti), dengan angka dan gambaran yang konkret. Taruh argumen terkuatmu di awal atau di akhir, jangan di tengah. Jawab keberatan sebelum pembaca mengajukannya (prolepsis: Some will say … In fact, …). Tutup dengan ajakan bertindak (call to action): siapa, apa, kapan. Bujuk, jangan memanipulasi: jangan menakut-nakuti, jangan memberi dilema palsu, jangan memakai pertanyaan menjebak.

guidedPractice.prompt: An NGO in Yogyakarta writes: 'Clean water is not a gift; it is a ___.' Complete the antithesis with ONE noun that contrasts with 'gift'.
guidedPractice.hint: A gift depends on someone's kindness. What can every person demand?

guidedPractice.prompt: Make the series parallel. Replace the last part with ONE adjective: 'The new library is quiet, modern and it has a lot of light.'
guidedPractice.hint: Three adjectives in a row: quiet, modern, ___.

guidedPractice.prompt: An op-ed opens: 'Not once has the council asked residents what they want.' Which C1 structure gives this sentence its emphasis? Write one or two words.
guidedPractice.hint: Look at the order of 'has' and 'the council'.

guidedPractice.prompt: Which appeal does this sentence from a petition rely on most: ethos, pathos or logos? 'The park absorbs about 40% of the rain that falls on this neighbourhood.'
guidedPractice.hint: A number and a cause-and-effect fact.

independentPractice.prompt: Rina's petition ends: 'We hope the council will think about this.' Make it a clear call to action. Complete with ONE verb: 'Please ___ against the car park plan at the council meeting on 12 March.'
independentPractice.hint: What do council members do at a meeting to make a decision?

independentPractice.prompt: A CEO writes to shareholders: 'Some will say we should have closed the Surabaya factory. In fact, it returned to profit in the last quarter.' What is the name of this technique, answering an objection before the reader raises it? Write one word.
independentPractice.hint: A Greek word that starts with 'pro-' (before).

independentPractice.prompt: Complete the rhetorical question with ONE word, so that the obvious answer is 'no': '___ any parent really want their child to play next to a six-lane road?'
independentPractice.hint: It's a yes/no question about 'any parent' (third person singular).

assessment.prompt: A practice campaign letter from an environmental NGO in Bogor ends: 'If we look after this river, this river will look after us.' Which device is it? Choose from: tricolon, anaphora, chiasmus, rhetorical question. Write the name.
assessment.rubric: Correct: chiasmus (A-B, then B-A: we … this river, this river … us). Antimetabole (the precise name when the same words come back reversed) = 100. 'antithesis' = 30 (the sentence is balanced, but there are no opposite ideas, and it isn't in the list). 'parallelism' = 30. 'tricolon', 'anaphora' or 'rhetorical question' = 0 (no three parts, no repeated opening, no question).

assessment.prompt: An op-ed in a Bandung newspaper argues for keeping a city park. Complete the antithesis with ONE word, the opposite of 'problem': 'This park is not a problem for the city to solve; it is an ___ for the city to seize.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: opportunity (problem ↔ opportunity; it fits 'an' and 'to seize'). 'chance' = 70 (the right idea, but 'an chance' doesn't fit the article). 'asset' = 60 (positive and fits 'an', but 'seize an asset' is unnatural and the contrast with 'problem' is weaker). 'opening' or 'advantage' = 60 (positive, but not the clear opposite of 'problem'). 'solution' = 20 (not the opposite idea here, and 'a solution to seize' makes no sense). Any negative word = 0.

assessment.prompt: An NGO campaign letter promises: 'With your donation, we will continue to train teachers, to build libraries and ___ fund scholarships.' Complete with ONE word so that the three parts stay parallel.
assessment.rubric: Correct: to (to train, to build, to fund: the same form three times). 'also' = 20 (grammatical, but it breaks the pattern of the series). 'we' = 20 (it makes the third part a new clause, so the series is no longer parallel). 'funding' or any form that doesn't fit before 'fund' = 0.

assessment.prompt: A letter to the Bandung city council begins: 'As a children's doctor who has worked in this district for fifteen years, I know these families well.' Which appeal does this sentence rely on most: ethos, pathos or logos? Write one word.
assessment.rubric: Correct: ethos (the writer shows why she can be trusted: her job and fifteen years of experience). 'credibility' = 100 (the meaning of ethos). 'pathos' = 20 ('I know these families well' adds a little warmth, but the sentence is built on the writer's authority). 'logos' = 0 (there's no evidence or reasoning yet).

assessment.prompt: Later in the same practice letter: 'Every afternoon, Bu Ani's grandchildren play under the old banyan tree in Taman Melati. If the car park is approved, that tree will be gone by June.' Which appeal does this rely on most: ethos, pathos or logos? Write one word.
assessment.rubric: Correct: pathos (a concrete image of real children and a tree they love, to make the reader feel the loss). 'emotion' / 'emotional appeal' = 100. 'logos' = 20 (there's a date, but no data or argument: the force is the image). 'ethos' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Pak Hasan is writing an op-ed against a plan to pave Taman Melati. He has three arguments: (A) the park is pleasant to walk in, (B) it protects about 300 homes from flooding, (C) it hosts a Sunday market. B is clearly his strongest. Where should he NOT put it: first, in the middle or last? Write the position.
acceptableAnswers: in the middle of the text
in the middle of the op-ed
assessment.rubric: Correct: in the middle (the strongest argument belongs first, where busy readers see it, or last, as a climax; in the middle it gets buried). 'first' or 'last' = 0 (those are the two good places). An answer that explains the reason as well = 100.

assessment.prompt: A leaflet against a new mall asks: 'Why does the council keep ignoring the people of Sukajadi?' Nobody has shown that the council ignores them. What do we call a question like this, which hides an unproven claim inside it? Write two words.
assessment.rubric: Correct: a loaded question (it assumes the council is ignoring people, so any answer seems to admit it). 'complex question' = 100 (the formal name of this fallacy). 'leading question' = 50 (close: it pushes towards an answer, but the point here is the hidden claim). 'rhetorical question' = 30 (it looks like one, but a fair rhetorical question has an obvious, true answer; this one smuggles in an unproven claim). 'false dilemma' or 'fear-mongering' = 0.

blocks.text:
At C1 you learnt to build an argument that holds up: a clear position, reasons, evidence, a fair counter-argument and a rebuttal. **Persuasive writing** uses all of that, but its goal is different: not only to show that you're right, but to make a particular reader **agree and act**. You'll meet it in:
- an **op-ed** (*artikel opini* in a newspaper or on a news site),
- a **petition** (*petisi*) to the city council,
- an **NGO campaign letter** asking for donations or support,
- a **CEO's letter to shareholders** (*surat CEO kepada pemegang saham*) explaining a difficult year.

A **rhetorical device** (*gaya bahasa retoris*) is a pattern of words that makes an idea easier to notice, remember or feel. You may remember similar names from **majas** in Bahasa Indonesia lessons: *anafora, antitesis, klimaks, kiasmus, majas retoris*. The ideas are close, but in this lesson we follow the English definitions.

**Essay or persuasive text?** An academic essay (C1) ends with your position and hedges its claims carefully: no call to action. A persuasive text may end with a **call to action** (*ajakan bertindak*: exactly what the reader should do) and uses more devices. It still needs evidence and honest claims: a device makes a good argument stronger, but it can't save a weak one.

id.text:
Di C1 kamu sudah belajar membangun argumen yang kokoh: posisi yang jelas, alasan, bukti, argumen tandingan yang adil dan bantahannya. **Tulisan persuasif** memakai semua itu, tapi tujuannya berbeda: bukan hanya menunjukkan bahwa kamu benar, tapi membuat pembaca tertentu **setuju dan bertindak**. Kamu akan menemuinya di:
- **op-ed** (*artikel opini* di koran atau situs berita),
- **petition** (*petisi*) kepada dewan kota,
- **NGO campaign letter** (surat kampanye LSM) yang meminta donasi atau dukungan,
- **CEO's letter to shareholders** (*surat CEO kepada pemegang saham*) yang menjelaskan tahun yang sulit.

**Rhetorical device** (*gaya bahasa retoris*) adalah pola kata yang membuat sebuah ide lebih mudah diperhatikan, diingat atau dirasakan. Mungkin kamu ingat nama-nama yang mirip dari pelajaran **majas** di Bahasa Indonesia: *anafora, antitesis, klimaks, kiasmus, majas retoris*. Idenya dekat, tapi di pelajaran ini kita mengikuti definisi bahasa Inggris.

**Esai atau teks persuasif?** Esai akademik (C1) diakhiri dengan posisimu dan klaimnya diperhalus dengan hati-hati: tanpa ajakan bertindak. Teks persuasif boleh diakhiri dengan **call to action** (*ajakan bertindak*: apa persisnya yang harus dilakukan pembaca) dan memakai lebih banyak gaya bahasa. Tetap saja, teks itu butuh bukti dan klaim yang jujur: gaya bahasa membuat argumen yang bagus jadi lebih kuat, tapi tidak bisa menyelamatkan argumen yang lemah.

blocks.prompt: Which of these texts would normally end with a call to action?
options: A petition to the city council
The literature review in a research report
blocks.explain: A petition exists to make the council do something, so it ends by saying exactly what (and when). An academic essay ends with its position, and a literature review summarises research: neither asks the reader to act.

id.prompt: Teks mana yang biasanya diakhiri dengan ajakan bertindak (call to action)?
id.explain: Petisi dibuat supaya dewan kota melakukan sesuatu, jadi ditutup dengan menyebutkan persis apa (dan kapan). Esai akademik ditutup dengan posisi penulis, dan tinjauan pustaka merangkum penelitian: keduanya tidak meminta pembaca bertindak.

material.title: Rhythm and build: tricolon, anaphora, parallelism, climax

blocks.text:
**Tricolon**, often called **the rule of three** (*aturan tiga*): three parallel parts. Three feels complete and is easy to remember; you'll find it in many political speeches and advertisements, and you used it in C1 presentations. *The new bus lane will make our trips faster, cheaper and safer.*

**Anaphora** (*anafora*): the same words at the **start** of several sentences or clauses. *We need shade. We need clean air. We need a place where our children can run.*

**Parallelism** (*struktur sejajar*): every item in a series has the **same grammatical form**: three adjectives, three *to* + verb, three clauses.
- ✓ *to protect, to cool and to connect*
- ✗ *to protect, cooling and connection*

**Climax** (*klimaks*): order the items from **weakest to strongest**, so the most important one comes last, where it lands hardest. *It will cost us money, it will cost us time, and it will cost our children their health.* (This sentence is a tricolon, an anaphora and a climax at once: devices often work together.)

**Inversion for emphasis** (C1): *Never has this neighbourhood needed a park more.* / *Not only does the park cool the streets; it also protects our homes from floods.* Use it once, at a key moment, in formal writing.

id.text:
**Tricolon**, sering disebut **the rule of three** (*aturan tiga*): tiga bagian yang sejajar. Tiga terasa lengkap dan mudah diingat; kamu akan menemukannya di banyak pidato politik dan iklan, dan kamu sudah memakainya di presentasi C1. *The new bus lane will make our trips faster, cheaper and safer.*

**Anaphora** (*anafora*): kata yang sama di **awal** beberapa kalimat atau klausa. *We need shade. We need clean air. We need a place where our children can run.*

**Parallelism** (*struktur sejajar*): setiap bagian dalam satu deretan punya **bentuk tata bahasa yang sama**: tiga kata sifat, tiga *to* + kata kerja, tiga klausa.
- ✓ *to protect, to cool and to connect*
- ✗ *to protect, cooling and connection*

**Climax** (*klimaks*): urutkan dari yang **paling lemah ke yang paling kuat**, supaya yang terpenting datang terakhir, saat dampaknya paling terasa. *It will cost us money, it will cost us time, and it will cost our children their health.* (Kalimat ini sekaligus tricolon, anaphora dan climax: gaya bahasa sering bekerja bersama.)

**Inversi untuk penekanan** (C1): *Never has this neighbourhood needed a park more.* / *Not only does the park cool the streets; it also protects our homes from floods.* Pakai sekali saja, di saat yang penting, dalam tulisan formal.

rows.en: With your support, we trained 40 teachers, opened 12 libraries and reached 9,000 children.
rows.id: Dengan dukunganmu, kami melatih 40 guru, membuka 12 perpustakaan dan menjangkau 9.000 anak.
rows.note: tricolon with concrete numbers, smallest to largest

id.note: tricolon dengan angka konkret, dari yang terkecil ke yang terbesar

rows.en: This park is where our children play. This park is where our parents walk. This park is where our neighbourhood meets.
rows.id: Taman ini tempat anak-anak kita bermain. Taman ini tempat orang tua kita berjalan-jalan. Taman ini tempat warga kita berkumpul.
rows.note: anaphora: the same opening three times

id.note: anafora: pembuka yang sama tiga kali

rows.en: We ask the council to stop the plan, to review the flood data and to meet the residents.
rows.id: Kami meminta dewan kota menghentikan rencana itu, meninjau data banjir dan menemui warga.

id.note: struktur sejajar: to + kata kerja tiga kali

rows.en: Rarely has a single decision affected so many families.
rows.id: Jarang sekali satu keputusan berdampak pada begitu banyak keluarga.
rows.note: C1 inversion: has comes before the subject

id.note: inversi C1: has datang sebelum subjek

blocks.text: **Two traps.** (1) **Unparallel lists**, very common when we write fast: ✗ *The park is green, quiet and it has many trees.* ✓ *The park is green, quiet and shady.* (2) **Too much of a good thing**: a tricolon in every paragraph sounds like an advertisement, and readers start noticing the trick instead of the idea. One strong device at a key moment (the opening, the turning point, the ending) is usually enough.

id.text: **Dua jebakan.** (1) **Deretan yang tidak sejajar**, sangat sering terjadi saat kita menulis dengan cepat: ✗ *The park is green, quiet and it has many trees.* ✓ *The park is green, quiet and shady.* (2) **Kebanyakan**: tricolon di setiap paragraf terdengar seperti iklan, dan pembaca mulai memperhatikan triknya, bukan idenya. Satu gaya bahasa yang kuat di saat yang penting (pembuka, titik balik, penutup) biasanya sudah cukup.

blocks.prompt: Which sentence has a parallel series?
options: The plan is cheap, fast and it can be done this year.
The plan is cheap, fast and realistic.
The plan is cheap, speed and realistic.
blocks.explain: Cheap, fast and realistic are three adjectives: the same form. The first sentence switches to a whole clause (it can be done…), and the second puts a noun (speed) between two adjectives.

id.explain: Cheap, fast dan realistic adalah tiga kata sifat: bentuknya sama. Kalimat pertama tiba-tiba berganti menjadi klausa utuh (it can be done…), dan kalimat ketiga menaruh kata benda (speed) di antara dua kata sifat.

id.title: Irama dan bangunan: tricolon, anafora, struktur sejajar, klimaks

material.title: Contrast and questions: antithesis, chiasmus, rhetorical questions

blocks.text:
**Antithesis** (*antitesis*): two opposite ideas in a **balanced** pair, usually *not X but Y* or *not X; Y*. *This park is not a cost; it is an investment.* The contrast makes Y the idea the reader remembers.

⚠ **Not only X but also Y is not antithesis.** It **adds** Y and keeps X: *The park is not only a cost but also an investment* still says it's a cost. In Indonesian terms: *bukan … melainkan …* = antithesis; *tidak hanya … tetapi juga …* = addition.

**Chiasmus** (*kiasmus*): two words come back in **reverse order**, A-B then B-A. *Invest in your people, and your people will invest in you.* (*you* and *your people* change places.) It sounds clever, so use it once at most, and only when it's instantly clear.

**Rhetorical question** (*pertanyaan retoris*): a question you don't expect the reader to answer aloud, because the answer is obvious. *Who wants to breathe exhaust fumes on the way to school?* It pulls the reader in. It becomes **manipulative** when the 'obvious' answer isn't actually true or proven, or when a string of questions replaces evidence (see the last section).

id.text:
**Antithesis** (*antitesis*): dua ide yang berlawanan dalam pasangan yang **seimbang**, biasanya *not X but Y* atau *not X; Y*. *This park is not a cost; it is an investment.* Kontras itu membuat Y menjadi ide yang diingat pembaca.

⚠ **Not only X but also Y bukan antitesis.** Pola itu **menambah** Y dan tetap mempertahankan X: *The park is not only a cost but also an investment* tetap mengatakan bahwa taman itu biaya. Dalam bahasa Indonesia: *bukan … melainkan …* = antitesis; *tidak hanya … tetapi juga …* = penambahan.

**Chiasmus** (*kiasmus*): dua kata muncul lagi dengan **urutan terbalik**, A-B lalu B-A. *Invest in your people, and your people will invest in you.* (*you* dan *your people* bertukar tempat.) Kedengarannya cerdas, jadi pakai paling banyak sekali, dan hanya kalau langsung jelas maksudnya.

**Rhetorical question** (*pertanyaan retoris*): pertanyaan yang tidak perlu dijawab pembaca, karena jawabannya sudah jelas. *Who wants to breathe exhaust fumes on the way to school?* Pertanyaan ini menarik pembaca masuk. Pertanyaan retoris menjadi **manipulatif** kalau jawaban yang 'jelas' itu sebenarnya tidak benar atau belum terbukti, atau kalau deretan pertanyaan dipakai untuk menggantikan bukti (lihat bagian terakhir).

rows.en: We are not asking for charity; we are asking for a fair chance.
rows.id: Kami tidak meminta belas kasihan; kami meminta kesempatan yang adil.

id.note: antitesis: belas kasihan ↔ kesempatan yang adil

rows.en: The question is not whether we can afford the park, but whether we can afford to lose it.
rows.id: Pertanyaannya bukan apakah kita mampu membiayai taman itu, melainkan apakah kita sanggup kehilangannya.

rows.en: Good parks make good neighbours, and good neighbours make good parks.
rows.id: Taman yang baik membuat tetangga jadi baik, dan tetangga yang baik membuat taman jadi baik.

rows.en: Do we really want our children's only playground to be a car park?
rows.id: Apa kita benar-benar mau satu-satunya tempat bermain anak-anak kita menjadi tempat parkir?
rows.note: rhetorical question: the answer (no) is obvious

blocks.text: **Rhetorical questions with a busy decision-maker.** One rhetorical question can engage a council or a board; three in a row sound like a lecture, or like you have no evidence. English readers often answer a rhetorical question silently in their heads, so make sure the answer they give is the one you want.

id.text: **Pertanyaan retoris untuk pengambil keputusan yang sibuk.** Satu pertanyaan retoris bisa menarik perhatian dewan kota atau direksi; tiga berturut-turut terdengar seperti ceramah, atau seolah kamu tidak punya bukti. Pembaca berbahasa Inggris sering menjawab pertanyaan retoris dalam hati, jadi pastikan jawaban mereka memang jawaban yang kamu inginkan.

options: We will listen, we will learn and we will act.
Serve the community, and the community will serve you.
Who would say no to cleaner air?
blocks.explain: Serve the community … the community will serve you: the two ideas come back in reverse order (A-B, B-A). The first sentence is an anaphora and a tricolon; the third is a rhetorical question.

id.explain: Serve the community … the community will serve you: kedua ide muncul lagi dengan urutan terbalik (A-B, B-A). Kalimat pertama adalah anaphora sekaligus tricolon; kalimat ketiga adalah pertanyaan retoris.

id.title: Kontras dan pertanyaan: antitesis, kiasmus, pertanyaan retoris

blocks.text:
**1. Know your reader.** Who decides, and what do they care about? A city council: the budget, the law, voters. Shareholders: profit, risk, the long term. Donors: impact and trust. Write for that reader, not for yourself.

**2. Frame the problem** (*membingkai masalah*) in the reader's terms. To a budget committee, Taman Melati (a fictional park in Bandung) is not just 'a beautiful park' but 'the cheapest flood protection the district has'.

**3. Use the three appeals** (*tiga daya bujuk*, described by the Greek philosopher Aristotle):
- **ethos** (*kredibilitas*): why the reader should trust you: your experience, accurate sources, fairness to the other side;
- **pathos** (*emosi*): what the reader should feel: a true story, a concrete image, shared values;
- **logos** (*logika dan bukti*): why it makes sense: numbers, cause and effect, comparisons.
Strong texts combine all three, with logos carrying the weight.

**4. Be concrete.** *Many trees will be cut down* is easy to ignore; *212 trees, some older than the city hall, will be cut down* is not.

**5. Put your strongest argument first or last**, never buried in the middle: readers remember beginnings and endings best. Busy readers may read only your first paragraph, so first is often safest; last gives you a climax.

**6. Answer objections before the reader raises them.** This is called **prolepsis**: *Some will say a park is a luxury. In fact, …* It's the written form of 'concede and counter' from C1.

**7. End with a call to action**: who, what, by when.

id.text:
**1. Kenali pembacamu.** Siapa yang memutuskan, dan apa yang mereka pedulikan? Dewan kota: anggaran, hukum, pemilih. Pemegang saham: laba, risiko, jangka panjang. Donatur: dampak dan kepercayaan. Tulis untuk pembaca itu, bukan untuk dirimu sendiri.

**2. Bingkai masalahnya** (*frame the problem*) dari sudut pandang pembaca. Bagi komisi anggaran, Taman Melati (taman fiktif di Bandung) bukan sekadar 'taman yang indah', tapi 'pelindung banjir termurah yang dimiliki kawasan itu'.

**3. Pakai tiga daya bujuk** (*the three appeals*, dijelaskan oleh filsuf Yunani Aristoteles):
- **ethos** (*kredibilitas*): mengapa pembaca harus percaya padamu: pengalamanmu, sumber yang akurat, sikap adil terhadap pihak lain;
- **pathos** (*emosi*): apa yang harus dirasakan pembaca: kisah nyata, gambaran yang konkret, nilai bersama;
- **logos** (*logika dan bukti*): mengapa argumennya masuk akal: angka, sebab-akibat, perbandingan.
Teks yang kuat menggabungkan ketiganya, dengan logos sebagai penopang utama.

**4. Buat konkret.** *Many trees will be cut down* mudah diabaikan; *212 trees, some older than the city hall, will be cut down* tidak.

**5. Taruh argumen terkuatmu di awal atau di akhir**, jangan terkubur di tengah: pembaca paling ingat bagian awal dan akhir. Pembaca yang sibuk mungkin hanya membaca paragraf pertamamu, jadi di awal sering paling aman; di akhir memberimu klimaks.

**6. Jawab keberatan sebelum pembaca mengajukannya.** Ini disebut **prolepsis**: *Some will say a park is a luxury. In fact, …* Ini versi tertulis dari 'akui dulu, lalu balas' di C1.

**7. Tutup dengan ajakan bertindak (call to action)**: siapa, apa, kapan.

rows.en: I have lived next to Taman Melati for thirty years and have chaired the residents' association for ten.
rows.id: Saya sudah tinggal di sebelah Taman Melati selama tiga puluh tahun dan sudah memimpin paguyuban warga selama sepuluh tahun.
rows.note: ethos: why the writer can be trusted

rows.en: Last February, the park absorbed rain that would otherwise have flooded about 300 homes.
rows.id: Februari lalu, taman itu menyerap hujan yang kalau tidak, akan membanjiri sekitar 300 rumah.
rows.note: logos: a concrete number, cause and effect

rows.en: Every evening, the park is full of children whose flats have no garden.
rows.id: Setiap sore, taman itu penuh anak-anak yang rumah susunnya tidak punya halaman.

id.note: pathos: gambaran yang nyata dan konkret

rows.en: Some will argue that the district needs parking more than trees. Yet a car park would earn about Rp 150 million a year, while one flood costs the district billions.
rows.id: Sebagian orang akan berpendapat bahwa kawasan ini lebih butuh tempat parkir daripada pohon. Padahal tempat parkir hanya menghasilkan sekitar Rp150 juta setahun, sementara satu kali banjir merugikan kawasan ini miliaran rupiah.
rows.note: prolepsis: the objection is answered with evidence

rows.en: We ask the council to reject the car park plan at its meeting on 12 March.
rows.id: Kami meminta dewan kota menolak rencana tempat parkir itu dalam rapat tanggal 12 Maret.
rows.note: call to action: who, what, by when

blocks.text: **Three Indonesian habits to adjust.** (1) A long ceremonial opening (*Puji syukur …*, *Dengan hormat, sehubungan dengan …*): in an English petition or op-ed, the reader should know the problem and your ask within the first two or three sentences. (2) A vague ending (*Marilah kita bersama-sama menjaga …* → *Let's protect our park together!*): replace it with a specific ask. (3) Emotional intensity on the page (*SANGAT PENTING!!!*, capitals, many exclamation marks): in English, calm wording with precise numbers sounds far more credible.

id.text: **Tiga kebiasaan orang Indonesia yang perlu disesuaikan.** (1) Pembuka seremonial yang panjang (*Puji syukur …*, *Dengan hormat, sehubungan dengan …*): dalam petisi atau op-ed berbahasa Inggris, pembaca sudah harus tahu masalahnya dan permintaanmu dalam dua atau tiga kalimat pertama. (2) Penutup yang samar (*Marilah kita bersama-sama menjaga …* → *Let's protect our park together!*): ganti dengan permintaan yang spesifik. (3) Emosi yang meluap di atas kertas (*SANGAT PENTING!!!*, huruf kapital, banyak tanda seru): dalam bahasa Inggris, kata-kata yang tenang dengan angka yang tepat terdengar jauh lebih meyakinkan.

blocks.prompt: Which is the clearest call to action for the end of a petition?
options: We hope the council will think about this carefully.
Please email your council member by Friday 7 March and ask them to vote no on the car park plan.
Let's protect our beautiful park together!
blocks.explain: It says who (you), what (email your council member and ask for a no vote) and by when (Friday 7 March). The other two are hopes or slogans: the reader finishes reading and doesn't know what to do.

id.prompt: Mana ajakan bertindak (call to action) yang paling jelas untuk penutup sebuah petisi?
id.explain: Kalimat itu menyebutkan siapa (kamu), apa (kirim email ke anggota dewan dan minta mereka menolak) dan kapan (Jumat, 7 Maret). Dua lainnya hanya harapan atau slogan: pembaca selesai membaca tapi tidak tahu harus berbuat apa.

blocks.text:
Persuasion gives the reader good reasons and lets them decide. **Manipulation** pushes them with tricks that don't survive a careful look. A reader who notices one trick stops trusting everything else you wrote, so honesty and effectiveness point the same way. These tricks are called **fallacies** (*sesat pikir*). Three to name and avoid:
- **Fear-mongering** (*menakut-nakuti*): exaggerating a threat to scare the reader. ✗ *If this park goes, Bandung will drown.* ✓ *Without the park, about 300 homes will face a higher risk of flooding.*
- **False dilemma** (*dilema palsu*): offering only two options when there are more. ✗ *Either we sell the land, or the city goes bankrupt.* ✓ *Selling the land is one option; cutting the parking subsidy is another.* Not every *either … or …* is a false dilemma: only when other real options exist.
- **Loaded question** (*pertanyaan menjebak*): a question that hides an unproven claim inside it. ✗ *Why is the mayor hiding the real cost?* (it assumes he is hiding it) ✓ *Has the full cost been published?*

Two more you know from C1 debate: **attacking the person** instead of the argument, and the **bandwagon** (*ikut-ikutan*): *Everyone is signing, so you should too.*

**Emotion is not manipulation by itself.** A true story about a real family is fair pathos. It becomes manipulation when it's exaggerated, invented or used *instead of* evidence.

id.text:
Persuasi memberi pembaca alasan yang bagus dan membiarkan mereka memutuskan. **Manipulasi** mendorong mereka dengan trik yang tidak bertahan saat diperiksa dengan teliti. Pembaca yang menyadari satu trik akan berhenti memercayai semua hal lain yang kamu tulis, jadi kejujuran dan efektivitas sejalan. Trik-trik ini disebut **fallacies** (*sesat pikir*). Tiga yang perlu dikenali dan dihindari:
- **Fear-mongering** (*menakut-nakuti*): membesar-besarkan ancaman untuk menakuti pembaca. ✗ *If this park goes, Bandung will drown.* ✓ *Without the park, about 300 homes will face a higher risk of flooding.*
- **False dilemma** (*dilema palsu*): hanya menawarkan dua pilihan padahal ada lebih banyak. ✗ *Either we sell the land, or the city goes bankrupt.* ✓ *Selling the land is one option; cutting the parking subsidy is another.* Tidak setiap *either … or …* adalah dilema palsu: hanya kalau sebenarnya ada pilihan lain yang nyata.
- **Loaded question** (*pertanyaan menjebak*): pertanyaan yang menyembunyikan klaim yang belum terbukti. ✗ *Why is the mayor hiding the real cost?* (pertanyaan ini menganggap wali kota memang menyembunyikannya) ✓ *Has the full cost been published?*

Dua lagi yang kamu kenal dari debat C1: **menyerang orangnya**, bukan argumennya, dan **bandwagon** (*ikut-ikutan*): *Everyone is signing, so you should too.*

**Emosi bukan manipulasi dengan sendirinya.** Kisah nyata tentang keluarga yang benar-benar ada adalah pathos yang adil. Emosi menjadi manipulasi kalau dibesar-besarkan, dikarang, atau dipakai *sebagai pengganti* bukti.

blocks.text: **A quick test before you publish.** (1) Is every number true, and could you show where it comes from? (2) Would you still make this argument if the reader could check everything? (3) Have you described the other side fairly? (4) Have you offered real options, not just two? If the answer to any of these is no, fix it: it will make the text more persuasive, not less.

id.text: **Tes cepat sebelum kamu menerbitkan.** (1) Apakah setiap angka benar, dan bisakah kamu menunjukkan sumbernya? (2) Apakah kamu tetap akan memakai argumen ini kalau pembaca bisa memeriksa semuanya? (3) Sudahkah kamu menggambarkan pihak lain dengan adil? (4) Sudahkah kamu menawarkan pilihan yang nyata, bukan hanya dua? Kalau ada jawaban 'tidak', perbaiki: teksmu akan jadi lebih persuasif, bukan kurang.

options: The 2023 flood damaged 41 shops on Jalan Melati.
If the council approves this plan, nobody in Bandung will ever be safe again.
Some residents disagree with us, and their worries about parking are real.
blocks.explain: 'Nobody … will ever be safe again' exaggerates the threat far beyond any evidence, just to scare. The first sentence is a concrete, checkable fact; the third describes the other side fairly, which builds ethos.

id.explain: 'Nobody … will ever be safe again' membesar-besarkan ancaman jauh melampaui bukti apa pun, hanya untuk menakuti. Kalimat pertama adalah fakta konkret yang bisa dicek; kalimat ketiga menggambarkan pihak lain dengan adil, dan itu membangun ethos.

suggestedQuestions: Isn't using emotion in writing always a bit manipulative?
How many rhetorical devices should I use in one op-ed?
What's the difference between antithesis and chiasmus?
How do I write a persuasive letter to someone senior without sounding rude?

id.intro: Di C1 kamu sudah membangun argumen yang kokoh, membantah pihak lain dan memakai inversi untuk penekanan. Sekarang kamu akan membuat tulisanmu benar-benar **persuasif**: gaya bahasa retoris seperti aturan tiga (rule of three), anafora, antitesis dan kiasmus, tiga daya bujuk (ethos, pathos, logos), dan struktur yang jelas yang ditutup dengan ajakan bertindak, semuanya tanpa melewati batas menjadi manipulasi. Pemanasan: apa yang bisa membuatmu mau menandatangani sebuah petisi?
suggestedQuestions: Bukankah memakai emosi dalam tulisan selalu agak manipulatif?
Berapa banyak gaya bahasa retoris yang sebaiknya saya pakai dalam satu op-ed?
Bagaimana cara menulis surat persuasif kepada orang yang lebih senior tanpa terdengar kasar?

assessment.rh-1: Sebuah surat kampanye latihan dari LSM lingkungan di Bogor ditutup dengan: 'If we look after this river, this river will look after us.' Gaya bahasa apa itu? Pilih dari: tricolon, anaphora, chiasmus, rhetorical question. Tulis namanya.
assessment.rh-2: Sebuah op-ed di koran Bandung mendukung agar sebuah taman kota dipertahankan. Lengkapi antitesisnya dengan SATU kata bahasa Inggris, lawan dari 'problem': 'This park is not a problem for the city to solve; it is an ___ for the city to seize.'
assessment.rh-3: Surat kampanye sebuah LSM berjanji: 'With your donation, we will continue to train teachers, to build libraries and ___ fund scholarships.' Lengkapi dengan SATU kata supaya ketiga bagiannya tetap sejajar.
assessment.rh-4: Sebuah surat kepada dewan kota Bandung dibuka dengan: 'As a children's doctor who has worked in this district for fifteen years, I know these families well.' Daya bujuk mana yang paling diandalkan kalimat ini: ethos, pathos atau logos? Tulis satu kata.
assessment.rh-5: Di bagian berikutnya dari surat latihan yang sama: 'Every afternoon, Bu Ani's grandchildren play under the old banyan tree in Taman Melati. If the car park is approved, that tree will be gone by June.' Daya bujuk mana yang paling diandalkan bagian ini: ethos, pathos atau logos? Tulis satu kata.
assessment.rh-6: Pak Hasan menulis op-ed yang menolak rencana mengaspal Taman Melati. Dia punya tiga argumen: (A) taman itu nyaman untuk jalan-jalan, (B) taman itu melindungi sekitar 300 rumah dari banjir, (C) taman itu menjadi tempat pasar hari Minggu. Jelas B argumen terkuatnya. Di mana dia TIDAK boleh menaruhnya: first (di awal), in the middle (di tengah) atau last (di akhir)? Tulis posisinya dalam bahasa Inggris.
assessment.rh-7: Sebuah selebaran yang menolak mal baru bertanya: 'Why does the council keep ignoring the people of Sukajadi?' Belum ada yang membuktikan bahwa dewan kota mengabaikan mereka. Apa nama pertanyaan seperti ini, yang menyembunyikan klaim yang belum terbukti di dalamnya? Tulis dua kata dalam bahasa Inggris.
